text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV 2 - Elevated KMS API latency observed in us-west-2 and us-east-1 (regions with busy signing traffic). Symptoms: new instance boot failures decrypting secrets, request signing timeouts causing 5xx on a subset of outbound requests. Auto-retries increasing downstream latency. Alerting thresholds crossed at 1835555400.

sara: Ack. Paging oncall. Mike, you on shift? I'm marking customer-impacting and will start an incident channel thread.

mike: Oncall here, looking. Can someone paste the startup error lines?

jen: Paste from a failed node boot log:
```
2026-03-15T02:45:12Z error: kms: Sign failed: context deadline exceeded (failed after 2 retries)
2026-03-15T02:45:12Z fatal: unable to decrypt /etc/secrets/app-creds.json: kms: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = server shutdown
```

mike: OK that's consistent with elevated latency/timeouts to KMS. Cloud metrics show 4xx/5xx spiking and increased p95 latency for kms:Sign in us-west-2. Rolling nodes trying to fetch secrets are timing out.

cory: Impact summary from infra side: autoscaler is still bringing up nodes to meet demand; ~35% of new nodes fail to reach Ready due to secret decrypt failures, causing extra churn and higher load. If churn continues we'll hit capacity problems in Dedicated pools.

aaron: Customer-reported noise: ticket #C-2147 - "500 errors on inference requests". Support sees errors correlated with signing failures around 02:45-03:05 UTC. Rough estimate: ~8% of requests returned 5xx across hosted API in us-west-2.

sara: Immediate mitigations we should consider (low-risk first):
- pause autoscaling / stop new node launches in affected AZs
- enable cached secret fallback for currently healthy nodes
- route new traffic to unaffected regions (us-central1) where possible
- open vendor ticket and get ETA

mike: Running these now. Patch to stop ASG scale-up for nodepool-west: 
```bash
# temp suspend scale-up via kubectl for cluster-autoscaler
kubectl patch deployment cluster-autoscaler -n kube-system --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/replicas","value":0}]'
```
Applying pinned for 2m...

jen: Also toggling REDWOOD_KMS_CACHE to enabled for api-deployments to use local cached keys for 1h TTL. Patch we use in rollout pipeline:
```yaml
env:
  - name: REDWOOD_KMS_CACHE_ENABLED
    value: "true"
  - name: REDWOOD_KMS_CACHE_TTL
    value: "3600"
```
Should reduce signing calls by ~60% for short term.

cory: Another option: switch artifact access to presigned URLs so model downloads don't hit KMS for each request. That will require a short deploy but could be targeted to the busiest services.

aaron: Noted for customer comms: preparing status page blurb saying "ongoing elevated KMS latency causing intermittent 5xx on inference in us-west-2; mitigation in progress. We'll update within 30 min."

aws-kms-support-bot: AWS Support ticket 987654321 created by Redwood. Initial response: "We're seeing increased control-plane throttling in us-west-2 affecting KMS sign/verify ops. Our teams are investigating. No ETA yet."

mike: Thanks. I'm running a quick canary in us-central by switching routing for low-risk traffic. Also enabling aggressive exponential backoff for KMS calls in the runtime (client-side) to avoid hammering. Patch: `KMS_MAX_RETRIES=6` and `KMS_BACKOFF_MS=200`.

sara: Good. Can we also make sure deploys are paused? I don't want a failed rollout during this.

jen: Deploys are paused. Also put a healthcheck override so existing nodes won't be evicted if they fail decrypt briefly. We're effectively allowing the in-memory secrets to persist until AWS resolves.

cory: Monitoring: adding dashboard panel for KMS sign latency + failed decrypts per minute. Alerting thresholds loosened temporarily to avoid noisy paging, but we're keeping a persistent dashboard tile.

aaron: Customer impact estimate: Affected users ~12% of traffic in us-west-2, error rate bump to 6-8% for short windows. Most customers see degraded latency rather than full outage. Proactive emails drafted for top 20 accounts.

mike: Vendor says investigating. I'm leaving a trace-level log to collect all KMS sign latencies for next hour and will attach to the support ticket. Also collecting node boot logs and stack traces.

sara: Handoff plan: I'm handing overnight to Mike at 1835555800. Mike, you own the pager and vendor comms. Please update the internal status page and escalate to AWS if we see additional degradation. I'll follow up in the morning with post-incident ops notes. :white_check_mark:

mike: Taking over. I'll keep this thread updated every 15-20m or on critical changes. Current state: autoscaling paused, cached-secret fallback enabled, traffic routing to us-central1 in effect, AWS ticket open. Next check in ~1835555940. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

incident-bot: Incident assigned -> owner: mike, severity: SEV 2, started_at: 2026-03-15T02:43:20Z

sara: Thanks team. After Mike confirms stabilization we'll prepare a short postmortem and customer FAQ steps (how to mitigate at client side if they hit 5xx).

mike: Update @everyone - initial stabilization seen: failed decrypts dropped from 35% to 6% after cache toggle and scale-down. AWS still investigating. Will update status and close once error rate <1% for 30m.

aws-kms-support-bot: Update on ticket 987654321: AWS control plane team applied mitigation in the region; we are monitoring for normalized latency. Please share if you observe re-occurrence.

mike: Noted. If latency is back to normal we'll re-enable autoscaling and roll caches back. If AWS doesn't fully resolve within 60m we'll consider longer-term mitigations: regional routing by default and pre-warmed cached decrypt service.

sara: Handoff complete. Mike owns incident until cleared. Good work. :thumbsup:
